items.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: She was in “Finian’s Rainbow” and she scatted and she sang with Leo Watson.

ctx.x: Oh Ella — yes I’ve read the name.
She was in “Finian’s Rainbow” and she scatted and she sang with Leo Watson.
Did you get into films out there at that time?

items.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I heard things like the Spirits of Rhythm, Leo Watson. She sang with them.

ctx.x: So I’m unsure if that was really a catalyst, or maybe just a reawakening.

I’ll tell you something. She was a bad – in the theater, she was a very strange combination of charming the birds off the trees or cuttin’ you down. But when I listened to her, I cried. She was a wonderful interpreter of lyrics. She did Glocca Morra. It’s said that – it was said that Jack Kennedy, when he heard of his – it was some big event that happened. The death of someone, his sister or whatever – that he would just spend hours listening to my aunt sing this, about Glocca Morra, Ireland. It made him weep.…

It also says at this time you were taken around to the various clubs, the 21, Stork Club, other things on that trip, which I guess only increased your infatuation and love for New York, presumably? No?
